item: A Stop pressed and cleared again inside one request's flight is still a Stop: the kill-switch engagement epoch (robots read, law tracker)
summary: R614, the engagement epoch R327 left as a stated limit (OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 item 17, adopted in R412). A recorder that reads the kill switch after its request (R320) saw a clear switch when the operator pressed Stop and went back online inside the request's flight, and stored the Stop as the target's failure: measured with the production fetcher on *.example hosts (export-lane/law-switch-sweep-2026-10-27, S5 and S6), the host's robots.txt cached as unreachable for 3,600 s and written to the sidecar, and a tracked law document's check stamped, which keeps it away for 24 h. activate_kill_switch() now bumps a module counter after it sets the switch, under a lock; kill_switch_epoch() is captured before a request and kill_switch_engaged_since(epoch) is true when the switch is engaged now or was engaged at any moment since. The two recorders R614 (3) names use it: EthicalFetcher._get_robots raises the refusal by name and caches and persists nothing, and track_document gives the check time back on its FetchError and other-error branches; the returned offline key and the skipped_offline tally stay decided by the refusal sentence, as when the switch is still engaged (R320). The other readers (feed pass, crawl rung, archive backfill, sitemap enumeration, preflight) are the follow-up PR. Cost, stated: a real failure that shares its flight with a Stop is not recorded and is asked again next pass. tests/test_kill_switch_epoch.py (10 cases) drives make_fetcher() with the airplane socket guard armed, a request only ever made with the switch engaged: a Stop cleared inside the robots read caches nothing and is the refusal, a Stop cleared inside the page read stamps no law check, and the controls (a real unreachable host, a real 503 on robots and on the page, an OSError with no Stop) record as before; 9 of 9 mutants of the change are killed. Release-notes line: pressing Stop and going back online while a request was under way no longer marks that site's robots.txt as unreachable for an hour, or a tracked law as checked for a day.
